General education.

the Foundation against the conventional breadth areas

BreadthUnits by area

The Foundation set against the breadth areas general education is conventionally measured by. A course can serve more than one area; units are counted once per area, so the column does not sum to the degree.

AreaCoursesUnitsHow
Written communicationRHET 1104Line-edited writing every week in RHET 110, and written answers and essays in every Canon course.
Oral communication—0No standalone course. Every made thing is defended out loud, in seminar or at exhibition, from the first semester; CAP 402's public defense is the graduation-level assessment.
Quantitative reasoningMATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 210, MATH 22016Calculus, linear algebra, and probability and statistics, each taught physical before formal.
Natural science with laboratoryPHYS 110, PHYS 1208Mechanics and waves, with laboratory work on the sand, in the water, and at the bench.
Arts and humanitiesHUM 101, HUM 102, HUM 201, HUM 202, HUM 301, HUM 302, HUM 401, HUM 40216The Canon, every semester: text, film, and album as one conversation.
Social and behavioral sciencesHUM 201, RHET 210, SIG 3017Political and economic philosophy, epistemics and propaganda, and the sociology of scenes. Thin by conventional standards; stated here rather than stretched.
ComputationCS 110, CS 120, CS 210, CS 22016Programming, machine organization, algorithms, and machine learning.
Status

A working framework, not an authorized degree. SDIT is in its founding phase and is not yet authorized to grant degrees; where authorization stands is published in full. The curriculum is open and free to take.
